nodes.name: Pt thin-film electrode preparation
nodes.procedure: The Pt thin-film electrode deposited on the Au substrate was first prepared through the galvanostatic method. The Pt thin-film electrode was deposited on a gold substrate using galvanostatic electrodeposition.

nodes.description: HER performance evaluation in alkaline KOH solution
nodes.source_text: HER polarization curves measured at 5 mV/s in Ar-saturated 0.1 M KOH for Pt, PtRu-low, and PtRu-high electrodes. The ratio of the current densities of PtM electrodes to that of Pt (denoted (j_PtM / j_Pt)_geo) at -0.035 V versus RHE.

nodes.description: HER performance evaluation of Mo-decorated Pt in alkaline KOH solution
nodes.source_text: Depositing Mo adatoms onto the Pt surface exhibits inhibition effect on the alkaline HER activity. The too-strong surface oxophilicity induced by Mo decoration triggered the PZC elevation for the Pt electrode and therewith the greater deviation of the reaction potential from PZC, which further resulted in the overly strong interfacial electric field and rigidity as well as the obstructed hydrogen bonding structure and eventually the negative effect on HER kinetics.

nodes.description: HER performance evaluation of Ru-decorated Pt in alkaline KOH solution
nodes.source_text: Depositing Ru adatoms onto the Pt surface exhibits a promotion effect on the alkaline HER activity. The moderate surface oxophilicity conferred by Ru decoration can effectively lower the electrode PZC, thus enabling a favorable interfacial environment and enhanced activity.

nodes.description: HER performance evaluation of Rh-decorated Pt in alkaline KOH solution
nodes.source_text: The decoration of Pt with low-coverage Rh (i.e., PtRh-low) also exhibits the ability to significantly promote HER activity, while the activity instead decayed when the Pt surface was completely covered by Rh in the PtRh-high electrode. The moderate surface oxophilicity conferred by Rh decoration can effectively lower the electrode PZC, thus enabling a favorable interfacial environment and enhanced activity.

nodes.description: HER performance evaluation of Au-decorated Pt in alkaline KOH solution
nodes.source_text: The opposite is true for Mo and Au decorations. The too-weak surface oxophilicity induced by Au decoration triggered the PZC elevation for the Pt electrode and therewith the greater deviation of the reaction potential from PZC, which further resulted in the overly strong interfacial electric field and rigidity as well as the obstructed hydrogen bonding structure and eventually the negative effect on HER kinetics.

nodes.description: In situ ATR-SEIRAS spectroscopy of interfacial water on Mo-decorated Pt
nodes.source_text: In situ ATR-SEIRAS spectra measured from -0.05 to 0.20 V in 0.1 M KOH for Pt, PtRu-low, and PtRu-high electrodes. Compared to the Mo-decorated Pt electrodes (red shift), the δ_H-O-H frequency exhibits evolution behavior. The hydrogen bonding of interfacial water molecules is weakened after the strongly oxyphilic Mo was deposited on the Pt electrode.

nodes.description: In situ ATR-SEIRAS spectroscopy of interfacial water on Ru-decorated Pt
nodes.source_text: The Rh- and Ru-decorated electrodes exhibits the completely opposite evolution behavior (i.e., blue shift) with the deposition coverage increasing. The Rh and Ru decoration with moderate oxophilicity contributes to strengthening the interfacial hydrogen bonding, thus accelerating the interfacial proton transfer and HER activity.

nodes.source_text: For Mo- and Au-decorated Pt electrodes, both the too-strong and too-weak surface oxophilicity bring about a higher interfacial electric field and a resultant more rigid interfacial environment, therefore reducing the alkaline HER rate.

nodes.description: DFT calculation of hydroxide adsorption free energy on pristine Pt
nodes.source_text: The hydroxide adsorption free energies (ΔG_OH*) on various transition metal adatoms were calculated via the DFT method. Figure 2f illustrates that the experimentally measured (j_PtM / j_Pt)_geo at -0.035 V of PtM-low electrodes in alkaline conditions follows a volcanic dependence on the binding strength of hydroxide.

nodes.description: AIMD simulation of potential of zero charge (PZC) on Au-decorated Pt
nodes.source_text: Mo- and Au-decorated electrodes with too-strong and too-weak oxophilicity give rise to the presence of abundant *OH species and the less O-down and more H-down water interactions, respectively, all which can increase PZC.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammetry shows typical polycrystalline Pt surface features with distinct underpotential deposition hydrogen (H_upd) peaks in the potential range 0–0.45 V and hydroxide adsorption/desorption peaks at ~0.80 V. Decorated PtM electrodes show decreased H_upd peak areas compared to pristine Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The cyclic voltammogram (CV) of the prepared Pt thin-film electrode in 0.1 M KOH (Figure 1b) shows the typical polycrystalline Pt surface features. The CVs of the PtM-low and PtM-high electrodes (Figures 1b and S4a-c) clearly show the distinct decrease of the area of underpotential deposition hydrogen (H_upd) peaks within the potential range from 0 to 0.45 V (from 0 to 0.2 V for PtMo electrodes) and the hydroxide adsorption/desorption peaks located at around 0.80 V compared to the undecorated Pt electrode.

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy in CO-saturated 0.1 M HClO₄ shows two CO adsorption peaks at ~2078 and 1875 cm⁻¹ assigned to top and bridge sites on Pt, with no CO adsorption on Au substrate.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEIRAS spectra measured in CO-saturated 0.1 M HClO₄ clearly exhibit two peaks at ~2078 and 1875 cm⁻¹ (Figure S2a), which are assigned to the C=O stretching modes of CO adsorbed on the top and bridge sites of the Pt surface, respectively, and no CO adsorption peak on Au that should be at ~2100 cm⁻¹ appears.

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic force microscopy images show Pt thin-film electrodes decorated with transition metals exhibit similar morphology characterized by islands of continuous Au nanoparticles approximately 50–100 nm in particle size with Pt or PtM nanoparticles densely wrapped around Au surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Exemplifying PtM-low, the atomic force microscopy (AFM) images show that the Pt thin-film electrodes decorated with various transition metals exhibit an overall similar morphology, which is characterized by islands of continuous Au nanoparticles, approximately 50–100 nm in particle size, with Pt or PtM nanoparticles densely wrapped around Au surfaces (Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: Hydrogen evolution reaction polarization curves measured at 5 mV/s in Ar-saturated 0.1 M KOH show that Ru and Rh decoration promote HER activity while Mo and Au decoration inhibit it. Current density ratios (j_PtM/j_Pt)_geo at −0.035 V versus RHE demonstrate volcano-type dependence on surface oxophilicity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figures 1c and S4d–f show the HER polarization curves measured in 0.1 M KOH, and Figure 1d gives the ratio of the current densities of PtM electrodes to that of Pt (denoted (j_PtM/j_Pt)_geo) at −0.035 V. It is apparent that depositing Ru adatoms onto the Pt surface exhibits a promotion effect on the alkaline HER activity, whereas the opposite is true for Mo and Au decorations.

nodes.characterization_summary: Density functional theory calculations of hydroxide adsorption free energies (ΔG_OH*) on various transition metal adatoms show a volcano-type relationship between surface oxophilicity and experimentally measured HER activity ratio (j_PtM/j_Pt)_geo at −0.035 V, with Rh at the apex.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2f illustrates that the experimentally measured (j_PtM/j_Pt)_geo at −0.035 V of PtM-low electrodes in alkaline conditions follows a volcanic dependence on the binding strength of hydroxide.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ attenuated total reflectance surface-enhanced infrared absorption spectroscopy measured from −0.05 to 0.20 V in 0.1 M KOH shows H–O–H bending vibration bands (δ_H-O-H) at ~1625 cm⁻¹ and O–H stretching vibration bands (ν_O-H) from 3000 to 3600 cm⁻¹. Rh and Ru decoration exhibit blue shift in δ_H-O-H frequency (strengthened hydrogen bonding), while Mo and Au show red shift (weakened hydrogen bonding). The difference in δ_H-O-H wavenumber between PtM-low and Pt shows volcano-type relationship with ΔG_OH*, with Rh at the apex.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a-c shows the SEIRAS spectra of interfacial water molecules on the pristine and Ru-decorated Pt thin-film electrodes in 0.1 M KOH, which clearly display the H–O–H bending vibration bands (δ_H-O-H) located at ~1625 cm⁻¹ and the O–H stretching vibration bands (ν_O-H) from 3000 to 3600 cm⁻¹. Besides, the inset depicts that the difference of δ_H-O-H wavenumber between PtM-low and Pt exhibits an obvious volcanic relation with ΔG_OH*, and Rh is at the apex of the volcano curve.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-SEIRAS analysis of O–H stretching wavenumber (ν_O-H) shows Stark tuning effect with potential sweep. Rh and Ru decoration increase Stark tuning rate (weaker interfacial electric field), while Mo and Au decoration decrease it (stronger interfacial electric field). Volcano-type relationship exists between Stark tuning rate ratio (R_PtM/R_Pt) and ΔG_OH*.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figures 3e and S12, the ν_O-H peaks on various electrodes display a distinct red shift as the potential swept positively due to the inherent dipole moment of water and its Stark tuning effect. Interestingly, one can note that with increasing the deposition coverage, the Stark tuning rate of interfacial water molecules gradually increases on Rh- and Ru-decorated electrodes, while it decreases on Mo- and Au-decorated electrodes (Figure S13).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations of PtAu/water, Pt/water, PtRh/water, PtRu/water, and PtMo/water interfaces show inverted volcano-type variation of potential of zero charge (PZC) with surface oxophilicity. Rh and Ru decoration lower PZC (moderate oxophilicity), while Mo and Au decoration increase PZC (too-strong and too-weak oxophilicity, respectively).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 4f shows that the PZC values on various electrodes exhibit an inverted volcano-type variation behavior with the surface oxophilicity, in which Au and Mo decoration indeed increases the PZC, while Rh and Ru decoration lowers the PZC compared to the pristine Pt electrode and Rh is at the apex of the volcano curve.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ab initio molecular dynamics simulations reveal that Rh- and Ru-decorated electrodes with moderate oxophilicity lead to more and stronger chemisorption of O-down water molecules, significantly reducing PZC. Mo- and Au-decorated electrodes with too-strong and too-weak oxophilicity show abundant *OH species and less O-down/more H-down water interactions, increasing PZC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Concretely, the Rh- and Ru-decorated electrodes with moderate oxophilicity lead to more and stronger chemisorption of O-down water molecules on the Rh and Ru sites, thus significantly reducing the PZC, whereas Mo- and Au-decorated electrodes with too-strong and too-weak oxophilicity give rise to the presence of abundant *OH species and the less O-down and more H-down water interactions, respectively, all which can increase PZC.

nodes.characterization_summary: DFT calculations determine stable adsorption states on electrode surfaces under reaction conditions. Surface Mo sites prefer abundant *OH species at the reaction potential, while Ru sites show only small amounts of *OH with water adsorption still dominant, consistent with Pourbaix phase diagrams.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figures S21 and S22, it was found that the surface Mo sites prefer to adsorb abundant *OH species at the reaction potential, while on the Ru sites, there merely could exist a small amount of *OH, and the water adsorption is still dominant. This is consistent with the Pourbaix phase diagrams of Mo and Ru elements, which show that Mo is in a certain oxidized state, while Ru is in the metallic state within the alkaline HER potential range.
